'''Prince''' is a block cipher targeting low latency, unrolled hardware implementations. It is based on the so-called FX construction.<ref>{{Cite book |doi = 10.1007/3-540-68697-5_20|chapter = How to Protect DES Against Exhaustive Key Search|title = Advances in Cryptology – CRYPTO '96|volume = 1109|pages = 252–267|series = Lecture Notes in Computer Science|year = 1996|last1 = Kilian|first1 = Joe|last2 = Rogaway|first2 = Phillip|isbn = 978-3-540-61512-5}}</ref> Its most notable feature is the '''alpha reflection''': the decryption is the encryption with a related key which is very cheap to compute. Unlike most other "lightweight" ciphers, it has a small number of rounds and the layers constituting a round have low logic depth. As a result, fully unrolled implementation are able to reach much higher frequencies than [[Advanced Encryption Standard|AES]] or [[PRESENT (cipher)|PRESENT]]. According to the authors, for the same time constraints and technologies, PRINCE uses 6–7 times less area than PRESENT-80 and 14–15 times less area than AES-128.<ref name=paper>{{cite journal|first1=Julia|last1=Borghoff|first2=Anne|last2=Canteaut|author2-link=Anne Canteaut|first3=Tim|last3=Guneysu|first4=Elif|last4=Bilge Kavun|first5=Miroslav|last5=Knezevic|first6=Lars R.|last6=Knudsen|first7=Gregor|last7=Leander|first8=Ventzislav|last8=Nikov|first9=Christof|last9=Paar|first10=Christian|last10=Rechberger|first11=Peter|last11=Rombouts|first12=Søren S.|last12=Thomsen|first13=Tolga|last13=Yalcın|title=PRINCE – A Low-latency Block Cipher for Pervasive Computing Applications|url=http://eprint.iacr.org/2012/529.pdf}}</ref>

==Overview==
{{More citations needed section|date=May 2024}}
The block size is 64 bits and the key size is 128 bits. The key is split into two 64 bit keys <math>K_{0}</math> and <math>K_{1}</math>. The input is XORed with <math>K_{0}</math>, then is processed by a core function using <math>K_{1}</math>. The output of the core function is xored by <math>K'_{0}</math> to produce the final output (<math>K_{0}'</math> is a value derived from <math>K_{0}</math>). The decryption is done by exchanging <math>K_{0}</math> and <math>K'_{0}</math> and by feeding the core function with <math>K_{1}</math> xored with a constant denoted alpha.<ref>{{Cite book |title=Advances in cryptology--ASiACRYPT 2012: 18th international conference on the theory and application of cryptology and information security, Beijing, China, December 2-6, 2012 proceedings |date=2012 |publisher=Springer |isbn=978-3-642-34961-4 |editor-last=International Conference on the Theory and Application of Cryptology and Information Security |series=Lecture notes in computer science |location=Heidelberg New York}}</ref>

The core function contain 5 "forward" rounds, a middle round, and 5 "backward" rounds, for 11 rounds in total. The original paper mentions 12 rounds without explicitly depicting them; if the middle round is counted as two rounds (as it contains two nonlinear layers), then the total number of rounds is 12.

A forward round starts with a round constant XORed with <math>K_{1}</math>, then a nonlinear layer <math>S</math>, and finally a linear layer <math>M</math>. The "backward" rounds are exactly the inverse of the "forward" rounds except for the round constants.

The nonlinear layer is based on a single 4-bit [[S-box]] which can be chosen among the affine-equivalent of 8 specified S-boxes.

The linear layer consists of multiplication by a 64x64 matrix <math>M'</math> and a shift row similar to the one in [[Advanced Encryption Standard|AES]] but operating on 4-bit nibbles rather than bytes.

<math>M'</math> is constructed from 16x16 matrices <math>M_{0}</math> and <math>M_{1}</math> in such a way that the multiplication by <math>M'</math> can be computed by four smaller multiplications, two using <math>M_{0}</math> and two using <math>M_{1}</math>.

The middle round consists of the <math>S</math> layer followed by <math>M'</math> followed by the <math>S^{-1}</math> layer.

==Cryptanalysis==
To encourage [[cryptanalysis]] of the Prince cipher, the organizations behind it created the {{cite web|url=https://www.emsec.rub.de/research/research_startseite/prince-challenge/|title=Prince challenge|access-date=2016-10-09|archive-date=2016-10-23|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161023201531/https://www.emsec.rub.de/research/research_startseite/prince-challenge/|url-status=dead}}

The paper "Security analysis of PRINCE"<ref name="Security analysis of PRINCE">{{cite journal |last1=Jean |first1=Jérémy |last2=Nikolic |first2=Ivica |last3=Peyrin |first3=Thomas |last4=Wang |first4=Lei |last5=Wu |first5=Shuang |date=2013 |title=Security analysis of PRINCE |url=https://www.iacr.org/archive/fse2013/84240085/84240085.pdf |journal=[[Fast Software Encryption]]}}</ref> presents several attacks on full and round reduced variants, in particular, an attack of complexity 2<sup>125.1</sup> and a related key attack requiring 2<sup>33</sup> data.

A generic time–memory–data tradeoff for FX constructions has been published, with an application to Prince.<ref>{{cite journal|first1=Itai|last1=Dinur|title=Cryptanalytic Time-Memory-Data Tradeoffs for FX-Constructions with Applications to PRINCE and PRIDE|url=https://eprint.iacr.org/2014/656.pdf}}</ref> The paper argues that the FX construction is a fine solution to improve the security of a widely deployed cipher (like [[DES-X]] did for [[Data Encryption Standard|DES]]) but that it is a questionable choice for new designs. It presents a tweak to the Prince cipher to strengthen it against this particular kind of attack.

A [[Biclique attack|biclique cryptanalysis]] attack has been published on the full cipher. It is somewhat inline with the estimation of the designers since it reduces the key search space by 2<sup>1.28</sup> (the original paper mentions a factor 2).
<ref>{{cite journal|first1=Farzaneh|last1=Abed|first2=Eik|last2=List|first3=Stefan|last3=Lucks|title=On the Security of the Core of PRINCE Against Biclique and Differential Cryptanalysis|url=https://eprint.iacr.org/2012/712.pdf}}</ref>

The paper "Reflection Cryptanalysis of PRINCE-Like Ciphers" focuses on the alpha reflection and establishes choice criteria for the alpha constant. It shows that a poorly chosen alpha would lead to efficient attacks on the full cipher; but the value randomly chosen by the designers is not among the weak ones.<ref>{{cite journal|first1=Hadi|last1=Soleimany|first2=Céline|last2=Blondeau|first3=Xiaoli|last3=Yu|first4=Wenling|last4=Wu|first5=Kaisa|last5=Nyberg|first6=Huiling|last6=Zhang|first7=Lei|last7=Zhang|first8=Yanfeng|last8=Wang|title=Reflection Cryptanalysis of PRINCE-Like Ciphers|url=http://research.ics.aalto.fi/publications/bibdb2012/public_pdfs/FSE2013.pdf}}</ref>

Several meet-in-the-middle attacks have been published on round reduced versions.<ref name="Meet-in-the-Middle Attacks and Structural Analysis of Round-Reduced PRINCE">{{cite journal|first1=Leo|last1=Perrin|first2=P.|last2=Derbez|title=Meet-in-the-Middle Attacks and Structural Analysis of Round-Reduced PRINCE|url=https://eprint.iacr.org/2015/239.pdf}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|first1=Leibo|last1=Li|first2=Keting|last2=Jia|first3=Xiaoyun|last3=Wang|title=Improved Meet-in-the-Middle Attacks on AES-192 and PRINCE|url=https://eprint.iacr.org/2013/573.pdf}}</ref><ref>{{cite book|first1=A.|last1=Canteaut|author1-link=Anne Canteaut|first2=M.|last2=Naya-Plasencia|first3=B.|last3=Vayssière|title=Advances in Cryptology – CRYPTO 2013 |chapter=Sieve-in-the-Middle: Improved MITM Attacks |series=Lecture Notes in Computer Science |year=2013 |volume=8042 |pages=222–240 |doi=10.1007/978-3-642-40041-4_13 |isbn=978-3-642-40040-7 }}</ref>

An attack in the multi-user setting can find the keys of 2 users among a set of 2<sup>32</sup> users in time 2<sup>65</sup>.<ref>{{cite journal|first1=Pierre-Alain|last1=Fouque|first2=Antoine|last2=Joux|first3=Chrysanthi|last3=Mavromati|title=Multi-user collisions: Applications to Discrete Logs, Even-Mansour and Prince|url=https://eprint.iacr.org/2013/761.pdf}}</ref>

An attack on 10 rounds with overall complexity of 118.56 bits has been published.<ref>{{cite journal|first1=Anne|last1=Canteaut|author1-link=Anne Canteaut|first2=Thomas|last2=Fuhr|first3=Henri|last3=Gilbert|first4=Maria|last4=Naya-Plasencia|first5=Jean-René|last5=Reinhard|title=Multiple Differential Cryptanalysis of Round-Reduced PRINCE|url=https://eprint.iacr.org/2014/089.pdf}}</ref>

An attack on 7 rounds with time complexity of 2<sup>57</sup> operations has been published.<ref name="Practical Attacks on the Round-reduced PRINCE">{{cite journal|first1=P.|last1=Morawiecki|title=Practical Attacks on the Round-reduced PRINCE|url=https://eprint.iacr.org/2015/245.pdf}}</ref>

A differential fault attack has been published using 7 faulty cipher texts under random 4 bit nibble fault model.<ref>{{cite journal|first1=Ling|last1=Song|first2=Lei|last2=Hu|title=Differential Fault Attack on the PRINCE Block Cipher|url=https://eprint.iacr.org/2013/043.pdf}}</ref>

The paper "New approaches for round-reduced PRINCE cipher cryptanalysis"<ref name="New approaches for round-reduced PRINCE cipher cryptanalysis">{{cite journal|first1=R.|last1=Posteuca|first2=C.|last2=Duta|first3=G.|last3=Negara|title=New approaches for round-reduced PRINCE cipher cryptanalysis|url=http://www.acad.ro/sectii2002/proceedings/doc2015-3s/01-Posteuca.pdf}}</ref> presents boomerang attack and [[known-plaintext attack]] on reduced round versions up to 6 rounds.

In 2015 few additional attacks have been published but are not freely available.<ref>{{cite journal|first1=R.|last1=Posteuca|first2=G.|last2=Negara|title=Integral cryptanalysis of round-reduced PRINCE cipher|journal=Proceedings of the Romanian Academy. Series A. Mathematics, Physics, Technical Sciences, Information Science |volume=16 |year=2015 |url=https://www.ams.org/mathscinet-getitem?mr=3413385}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|first1=G.|last1=Zhao|first2=B.|last2=Sun|first3=C.|last3=Li|first4=J.|last4=Su|title=Truncated differential cryptanalysis of PRINCE|journal=Security and Communication Networks |volume=8|issue=16|pages=2875–2887|year=2015|doi=10.1002/sec.1213|s2cid=30147147 }}</ref>
